title: Components
subtitle: Function components, composition, the children prop, and component design
author: KERNAL Team

whyItExists.problem: Monolithic UIs are hard to maintain. If you build your entire page in one giant function, bugs are hard to find and elements can't be reused.
whyItExists.solution: Components break UI into small, self-contained, reusable pieces. Each component has a single responsibility. They compose like building blocks — a page is a tree of components.
whyItExists.whenToUse: Extract any repeated or logically isolated piece of UI into its own component. If a JSX block is getting complex (more than ~20 lines), it's a candidate for extraction.
whyItExists.whenNotToUse: Don't over-split. A tiny 3-line piece of JSX doesn't need its own component file. Find the right granularity — extract when there's genuine reuse or when the complexity hides in an inline block.

explainModes.beginner: A component is just a function that returns JSX. You can use one component inside another — this is called composition. If a section of your UI is repeated (like a card, or a button), make it its own component. Pass data to components using props (like HTML attributes).
explainModes.simple: Component = function that returns JSX. Must start with capital letter. Props = the 'input' to a component. children prop = whatever is between the component's opening and closing tags. Composition: <Layout><Header /><Main /></Layout>. Spread props: <Button {...buttonProps} />. Pure components: same props → same output, no side effects.
explainModes.standard: The component tree is a tree of function calls. React calls each function to get its JSX, recursively, building the full virtual DOM. Each component owns its subtree. Lifting state up: when two components need the same state, put it in their nearest common ancestor and pass it down as props. Prop drilling becomes a problem in deep trees — solve with Context (covered later).
explainModes.technical: React components must be pure: for the same props, same output; no side effects during render (use useEffect for side effects). Concurrent features (React 18) may call components multiple times in development (StrictMode) to catch accidental side effects. Component identity: React uses the component function reference and position in the tree to identify components across renders. If you define a component inside another, React creates a new 'type' every render — causing remounts. Always define components at the module level.
explainModes.deepDive: Component composition patterns: Slot pattern (children prop), compound components (multiple sub-components that share implicit state), render props (passing JSX as a function prop), higher-order components (HOCs, legacy). The children prop is just another prop — it's special only by convention. You can accept multiple 'slots': <Card header={<H1 />} footer={<Footer />} />. React.cloneElement lets you inject extra props into a child element — used in compound components.

questions.question: What is the children prop in React?
options: A special array of all child components in the application
Whatever JSX or content is placed between a component's opening and closing tags
A required prop that every React component must accept
The list of HTML child elements from the DOM
questions.explanation: The children prop receives whatever is placed between a component's opening and closing tags: <Card>This text becomes children</Card>. It can be text, JSX, other components, or arrays of elements. children is just a convention — technically it's a regular prop called 'children' that React automatically populates.

faq.q: How do I know when to extract a new component?
faq.a: Three signals: (1) Repetition — if you copy-paste the same JSX block twice, make it a component. (2) Complexity — if a JSX block is too long to scan at a glance, extract it. (3) Reuse — if the same UI pattern appears in different contexts. Start with fewer components and extract as complexity grows, rather than pre-splitting everything upfront.

examples: function Button({ variant, size, onClick, children }) — reusable button with variants
function Modal({ isOpen, onClose, title, children }) — slot-based modal component
function DataTable<T>({ data, columns, onRowClick }) — generic typed table
